subject: Request: accelerated capacity increase + early renewal discount
messages:

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Early renewal & capacity bump — initial proposal

Hi Liam,

Great catching up last week. Per our conversation, I pulled together an initial proposal for an accelerated renewal that also covers the extra capacity NovaFlow needs for Q3. High level:

- 3x baseline capacity for 12 months (billed monthly)
- Early renewal term (12 mo) in exchange for a committed discount and a one-time capacity credit
- Optional 6-month price-hold on the committed rate during the uplift period

I've attached a stub with the usage projection and a preliminary pricing model so you can sanity-check numbers. If you can confirm the capacity uplift target and whether you want the 6-month hold, I will turn this into a formal amendment for legal.

Attachments: NovaFlow_renewal_request_v2.xlsx (Excel)

Next steps: can we lock a 30-min call Wed to finalize the numbers?

Thanks,
Ben

Cc: contracts@novaflow.com, Helen Park <hpark@novaflow.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Early renewal & capacity bump — initial proposal

Ben,

Thanks — this is exactly the direction we discussed internally. Quick clarifications before a call:

1) Capacity: we need ~3x current committed throughput (peak tokens/sec) starting 1 Jul and for the next 12 months.
2) Price hold: critical for our forecasting. We'd prefer a 12-month hold at the agreed committed rate.
3) Discount: to get internal sign-off we'd need ~15–18% off current committed list price, or equivalent credits.

If you can sketch two options (12% + $150k credit with 12-month hold) vs (18% + $0 credit with 9-month hold) we'll present to procurement tomorrow. Also cc'ing contracts for any legal constraints.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.
— Liam
Liam O'Connor
VP, Platform Engineering | NovaFlow
liam.oconnor@novaflow.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Early renewal & capacity bump — internal ask from NovaFlow (ND-4281)

Marissa / Grace — forwarding NovaFlow's ask. TL;DR: 3x capacity uplift starting July, requests either (A) 12% discount + $150k credit + 12-mo hold OR (B) 18% discount + 0 credit + 9-mo hold. They prefer the 12-month hold.

My recommended play to protect margin while closing fast: propose Option A but move credit to be drawn over first 3 invoices (protects unit economics) and include a conditional burst pool at list for non-committed overage. Also require a 12-month committed term and DocuSign amendment.

Questions:
- Do we have room to do 12% + $150k credit?
- If not, would 10% + $200k credit be acceptable?

I've attached a quick sensitivity model. If I get a green light I will send the formal amendment and a DocuSign link.

Attachments: pricing_model_NovaFlow_v1.xlsx (Excel)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Early renewal & capacity bump — internal ask from NovaFlow (ND-4281)

Ben — thanks for the summary. A few notes from pricing & finance:

- We can support a firm 10% discount if we get the credit amortized against invoices (i.e., $125k applied over first 3 months). 12% starts to stretch margin unless we tighten burst billing.
- I like the idea of a 12-month price-hold only if we include a clause that any material model upgrades requiring higher-cost kernels are excluded (protects us).
- Legal will need the amendment to include an explicit usage floor and invoice true-up quarterly.

If we position the offer as: 10% + $125k amortized credit + 12-month limited price-hold (with upgrade carve-outs), I think we can get approval quickly and keep the deal economics intact.

Can you run the revised amendment and a margin sensitivity for the 10%/12% scenarios? If procurement pushes for 18% we should push back and offer a stepped discount that vests over committed usage thresholds.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Pricing & Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novaflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, contracts@novaflow.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Early renewal & capacity bump — proposal (Option A — revised)

Liam — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is a revised proposal reflecting our internal guidance:

Option A (revised):
- 12-month committed term starting 1 Jul
- 3x capacity uplift (as requested)
- 10% discount on committed units
- $125,000 credit amortized over the first 3 invoices
- 12-month limited price-hold (excludes material kernel/infra upgrades; details in amendment)
- Burst/overage billed at list (no discount)

I've also included a sensitivity workbook that shows net ARR and margin impact at different utilization rates. DocuSign amendment link here: https://www.docusign.com/en/documents/ND-4281-amendment

Attachments: pricing_model_NovaFlow_v1.xlsx (Excel), NovaFlow_usage_Q2.csv (CSV)

Can you confirm procurement is okay with the amortized credit and the burst billing? If so, I'll route for signature.
